turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Apply a thin uniform coat of Prussian blue or engineer's marking compound to the taper surface of a clean test arbor. Insert the arbor into the spindle taper bore and rotate by hand under moderate axial load for two to three turns, then withdraw the arbor and inspect the transfer pattern.

ground_truth.node_text: Apply a thin uniform coat of Prussian blue or engineer's marking compound to the taper surface of a clean test arbor. Insert the arbor into the spindle taper bore and rotate by hand under moderate axial load for two to three turns. Withdraw the arbor and inspect the transfer pattern; uniform contact over at least 75% of the taper length is required. A patchy or one sided pattern indicates taper bore damage, swarf contamination, or arbor misalignment.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Marking compound applied and test arbor rotated. The transfer pattern shows good uniform contact across the taper length.

ground_truth.node_text: Apply a thin uniform coat of Prussian blue or engineer's marking compound to the taper surface of a clean test arbor. Insert the arbor into the spindle taper bore and rotate by hand under moderate axial load for two to three turns. Withdraw the arbor and inspect the transfer pattern; uniform contact over at least 75% of the taper length is required. A patchy or one sided pattern indicates taper bore damage, swarf contamination, or arbor misalignment.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the taper contact pattern above 80 percent of taper area?

ground_truth.node_text: Taper contact pattern above 80% of taper area?

turns.utterance: Using a calibrated non contact tachometer, direct the sensor beam at a reflective strip on the spindle nose. Command each of the four test speeds from the machine controller and record the actual speed displayed by the tachometer. Calculate the percentage speed error at each commanded speed.

ground_truth.node_text: Using a calibrated non contact tachometer, direct the sensor beam at a reflective strip on the spindle nose. Command each of the four test speeds from the machine controller and record the actual speed displayed by the tachometer. Calculate the percentage speed error at each commanded speed and compare against the maximum speed accuracy tolerance in the spindle acceptance specification.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Tachometer readings recorded at all four test speeds. Speed errors calculated and all are within tolerance.

ground_truth.node_text: Using a calibrated non contact tachometer, direct the sensor beam at a reflective strip on the spindle nose. turns.utterance: No, the vibration readings at full rated speed are exceeding the warning limit in the Y axis.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Complete the following checks: reduce spindle speed to 50 percent rated and monitor vibration for two minutes, check whether vibration reduces at lower speed to indicate a balance issue, and inspect the spindle nose and toolholder taper for contamination or damage.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following checks: 1. Reduce spindle speed to 50% rated and monitor vibration for two minutes. 2. Check whether vibration reduces at lower speed to indicate a balance issue. 3. Inspect the spindle nose and toolholder taper for contamination or damage.

turns.utterance: Checks completed. Vibration does reduce at 50 percent speed, suggesting a balance issue. Spindle nose and taper appear clean with no visible damage.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following checks: 1. Reduce spindle speed to 50% rated and monitor vibration for two minutes. 2. Check whether vibration reduces at lower speed to indicate a balance issue. 3. Inspect the spindle nose and toolholder taper for contamination or damage.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Mount a dial test indicator against a precision reference mandrel clamped in the spindle. Zero the indicator and record the position as the cold datum. Run the spindle at operating speed for 30 minutes and record the indicator position at five minute intervals.

ground_truth.node_text: Mount a dial test indicator against a precision reference mandrel clamped in the spindle before starting the warm up cycle. Zero the indicator and record the position as the cold datum. Run the spindle at operating speed for 30 minutes and record the indicator position at five minute intervals. Note the total thermal displacement at stabilisation and compare against the thermal growth compensation value stored in the machine thermal model parameters.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Thermal growth test completed. Indicator readings recorded at each interval and total thermal displacement at stabilization documented.

ground_truth.node_text: Mount a dial test indicator against a precision reference mandrel clamped in the spindle before starting the warm up cycle. turns.utterance: Command the spindle orientation to the 0 degree reference position from the machine control panel. Mount a precision angular encoder or dial test indicator on an arm at a known radius and measure the angular error. Command orientation to 90, 180, and 270 degrees and measure the angular error at each position.

ground_truth.node_text: Command the spindle orientation to the 0 degree reference position from the machine control panel. Mount a precision angular encoder or a dial test indicator on an arm at a known radius and measure the angular error relative to the reference mark. Command orientation to 90, 180, and 270 degrees and measure the angular error at each position; compare all four readings against the spindle orientation accuracy specification.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Spindle orientation measurements completed at all four positions. Angular errors recorded for each commanded angle.

ground_truth.node_text: Command the spindle orientation to the 0 degree reference position from the machine control panel. turns.utterance: Fit a sealed test arbor with a coolant pressure gauge and flow indicator into the spindle taper. Start the coolant through spindle circuit at normal operating pressure and read the pressure gauge at the spindle taper outlet. Observe the flow indicator for steady flow.

ground_truth.node_text: Fit a sealed test arbor with a coolant pressure gauge and flow indicator into the spindle taper. Start the coolant through spindle circuit at the normal operating pressure. Read the pressure gauge at the spindle taper outlet and compare against the minimum required coolant through spindle pressure. Observe the flow indicator for steady flow; pulsing or absent flow indicates a blocked spindle check valve or a failing coolant pump.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Test arbor fitted and coolant circuit started. Pressure gauge and flow indicator readings recorded.

turns.utterance: Load the test piece material into the machine work holding and run the standard spindle test machining program. After machining, measure bore diameter at three depths and face flatness at four points using a coordinate measuring machine or precision gauges.

ground_truth.node_text: Load the test piece material, typically a 100 millimetre diameter aluminium or cast iron disc, into the machine work holding and run the standard spindle test machining program. The program bores a 50 millimetre diameter hole and faces the top surface. After machining, measure bore diameter at three depths and face flatness at four points using a coordinate measuring machine or precision gauges. Compare all results against the machined geometry tolerances in the spindle acceptance test plan.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Test piece machined and measurements completed. All bore diameters and face flatness readings recorded.
